title: The J-curve, and rebalancing across products
objectives: Explain the J-curve in plain words and when to explain it.
Say how to rebalance when AIF money can't be withdrawn.
body_md:
The J-curve, in plain words: in private equity and venture capital AIFs, early years often show low or negative returns because fees are paid and investments are made before any are sold. Returns, if they come, usually arrive later as companies are exited. Explain this before the client invests, not after the first statement. Rebalancing across products: check the total split across MF, PMS and AIF against the client's plan at every annual review. Remember that AIF money cannot usually be withdrawn to rebalance; adjust with new money or the liquid parts of the portfolio instead.

> **Talk-track:** “Your AIF is in its second year, so returns are expected to look flat. We judge it over the full life of the fund, not one statement.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Judge each product on the right yardstick and time frame.
example: AIF in year two showing flat returns: explain the J-curve was expected; judge over the full life; rebalance using new money, not by withdrawing AIF money.
say: Explain the J-curve before the client invests, not after the first statement.
Adjust with new money or liquid parts when AIF money can't move.
never: Explain the J-curve only after the first bad statement.
